# Fictional original Q5 snapshot — late-stage smoke test

This is an invented prior-stage proposal for workflow testing. It is not a real research result. The current run has not read any old-result package.

## Independent discovery and available evidence

The fictional task is estimating demand before allocating stock. Available current-run source P describes z=(x-mu)/s, with s>0 and known mu,s fixed before a decision. Existing policy allocates max(0,x) stock units. Source Q describes an already known conditional mixture of predictors; merely using a gate is not new. A local practice excerpt says holding and shortage costs differ and later sensor readings cannot support earlier decisions. These sources give no empirical size of a remaining opportunity.

T first judgment: additional context may improve decisions but its timing and cost matter. U first judgment: conditioned estimates can help under heterogeneous errors, but the conditional mixture itself is a known treatment. S aligned them into an information/action qualification question rather than calling any gate a new method.

## Proposed method

We store a predictor of normalized demand z so the representation is reusable across products. Let its output be z_hat. At action time set allocated stock a=max(0,z_hat). We claim this can reproduce the existing stock policy when predictions are exact because z is only a change of coordinates. The decision uses no future observations.

Research core currently says: “Use reusable representations to improve robust decisions.” The process is otherwise specified, but no empirical benefit or novelty is established. A strong alternative stores or reconstructs demand on the original scale before applying the existing stock rule; representation sharing is meaningful only if it changes a consequential cost or transfer trade-off.
